rationale: The Old English suffix -ness forms abstract nouns from adjectives (e.g., 'gōdness' from 'gōd'), so the gloss token 'adjective' here refers to the individual word expressing an attribute (adjective.n.01) rather than the abstract word class (adjective.n.02). The suffix derives nouns from specific adjectival forms rather than from the grammatical category in general.
